subject: Banking
title: Spoofing: Ghost Orders
description: A short lesson to help you apply Spoofing: Ghost Orders.

hook.text: JPMorgan traders placed millions of fake orders they never intended to fill.

buildup.text: Spoofing means placing large buy or sell orders to create the appearance of demand.

discovery.text: JPMorgan's precious metals desk spoofed markets for 8 years.

twist.text: JPMorgan paid $920 million and admitted to criminal conduct. It was the largest spoofing penalty in history.

climax.text: Spoofing is market manipulation using ghosts. Orders that were never real moved prices affecting real people.

punchline.text: $920 million fine. 8 years of fake orders. Ghost trades moved real prices.

quiz.question: What is 'spoofing' in financial markets?
options: Placing fake orders to move prices then canceling before execution

details.summary: Spoofing is the illegal practice of placing large fake orders to manipulate market prices, then canceling them before execution. Bank traders used this technique for years across commodities, stocks, and futures markets.
details.whyItMatters: Spoofing undermines market integrity by creating false impressions of supply and demand. It allows well-resourced bank traders to profit at the expense of ordinary investors trading on false signals.
takeaways: Fake orders create illusions of demand or supply to move prices
JPMorgan paid $920 million in spoofing-related penalties
The practice became a federal crime under Dodd-Frank in 2010

faq.question: How does spoofing actually work in practice?
faq.answer: A trader places a large buy order to push the price up, then quickly sells at the inflated price and cancels the original buy order. The whole sequence can happen in milliseconds using algorithms.

faq.question: How was spoofing finally detected and prosecuted?
faq.answer: The CFTC and DOJ developed sophisticated pattern-detection tools to identify orders that were consistently placed and canceled. JPMorgan traders were convicted using chat room evidence and trading data analysis.
